prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a continuous foreground brightness gradient across a curved conference table (0.3–1.5 m away) supporting two side-by-side laptops directly in front of the camera wearer at ~0.4–0.6 m (spaced ~0.1 m apart) and a tablet to their left at ~0.6 m, all within the wearer's arm's reach, alongside the wearer's brightly lit right hand (~0.3 m) over the right laptop keyboard and a neighbour's forearm entering at the bottom-right (~0.4 m). Behind the table's far edge, an empty chair back sits at ~1.5 m on the right while a person in a blue shirt sits ~2.0–2.5 m ahead-left facing left in profile (not looking at the wearer) with a tablet within their reach (~0.3 m in front of them), and a background desk row with monitors lies ~3.5–4.5 m behind them. Across frames 1 to 4, the scene geometry stays stationary while the wearer's right hand shifts slightly rightward onto the laptop corner and a left-side neighbour's arm (~0.5 m) recedes out of view before re-entering; in frame 5, the camera wearer turns sharply left, bringing two nearby people on the left into view—a partially visible face at the bottom-left corner in extreme close-up (~0.25–0.35 m, ~0.3 m from the next person) and a seated woman in a white shirt (~0.8–1.0 m away, facing and looking toward the wearer)—plus a distant seated person (~3.5 m) behind her. The depth map makes the continuous 3D surface recession of the tabletop and the exact depth layering between the foreground head (~0.3 m), mid-ground woman (~0.9 m), and background figures (2.0–3.5 m) much clearer than RGB alone. However, it is unreliable on dark background walls and distant monitors where depth collapses to uniform black, and it flattens thin structures like glasses and face masks onto surrounding surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground objects on the table, consistently labelling the two side-by-side laptops in front of the wearer (~0.4–0.6 m away, ~0.1 m apart) and the smaller tablet/laptop to their left (~0.6 m, within arm's reach of both the wearer and the person to the left), while segmenting the empty chair back behind the right laptop (~1.5 m) and the seated person in the blue shirt (~2.0–2.5 m ahead-left, facing left away from the wearer) along with their chair crest. Along the lower and left edges of frames 1 to 4, masks capture partially occluded body parts at ~0.3–0.6 m, including a left-side person's arm in frames 1 and 3, and the wearer's right hand and a right-side neighbour's arm in frames 3 and 4. In frame 5, as the camera turns left, the map segments five distinct people: the close-up head at the bottom-left (~0.3 m), the woman in the white shirt (~0.8–1.0 m, ~0.3 m behind the close-up head, facing and looking toward the wearer), the distant seated person behind her (~3.5 m), the blue-shirted person (~2.2 m on the right), and the wearer's raised right hand at the right edge (~0.3 m), while the right laptop is mostly cut off at the right border. Compared to RGB, the instance masks clearly separate overlapping foreground contours—such as distinguishing the wearer's hand mask from the adjacent neighbour's arm mask at the bottom-right and isolating small background monitors ('tv' at ~3.5–4.0 m). However, the map is unreliable across frames, missing the wearer's hand in frames 1–2 where it leaves a black hole in the right laptop mask, mislabelling the left tablet as 'book' in frame 5 and a nearby face mask/gap as 'cell phone' in frame 4, and hallucinating a 'person' label on the right laptop's screen corner in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, tracking the upper body, head, and arms of the seated person in the blue shirt (~2.0–2.5 m ahead-left) across frames 1 to 4, showing their torso angled left, head in left profile looking away from the camera wearer, left arm resting on the table toward a tablet within their reach (~0.3 m away), and right hand raised supporting their chin. In frame 2 only, a magenta hand skeleton appears at the bottom center (~0.3 m from the wearer), capturing the curled fingers of the camera wearer's right hand resting within reach on the right laptop's keyboard. Across frames 1 to 4, the blue-shirted person's skeleton remains stationary, whereas in frame 5 the camera turns left so that only the woman seated ~0.8–1.0 m away on the left is tracked, with her torso and facial keypoints oriented toward the camera wearer, her right arm resting across her lap, and her left elbow propped up with a magenta hand skeleton raised near her chin/neck. The skeleton map makes exact joint articulations, head orientation keypoints (eyes, ears, nose), and the chin-resting arm geometry immediately explicit without visual clutter from clothing or lighting. However, it is heavily unreliable for overall scene coverage, completely failing to detect the blue-shirted person, the very close face at the bottom-left (~0.3 m), and the distant background person (~3.5 m) in frame 5, while missing the wearer's hands in frames 1 and 3–5 as well as all truncated arms of the adjacent neighbours on the left and right edges.
